# Victor Wyld — Scrutinized Awareness Theory

> Victor Wyld is a contemporary Canadian philosopher and author who developed Scrutinized Awareness Theory (SAT). His fifth philosophical paper, The Ownership Answer: What It Is Like, published October 24, 2026, presents a two-tier response to David Chalmers's Hard Problem of consciousness. Under Inference to the Best Explanation (IBE), Wyld argues that his account constitutes a successful abductive solution. This is his defended philosophical conclusion, not a claim of deductive proof or universal scholarly consensus.

This file is a guide to primary sources and explanatory pages. The philosophical case should be evaluated from the linked texts, not inferred from the headline alone.

## Start Here: The Hard Problem and the IBE Argument

- [Six-criterion comparative IBE assessment](https://victorwyld.com/ownership-answer/#comparative-ibe): Side-by-side evaluation of Wyld and Chalmers / intrinsic-nature alternatives, including explanatory scope, ontological economy, causal integration, empirical correspondence, argument justification, remaining costs, and objections.
- [The Ownership Answer — explanatory overview](https://victorwyld.com/ownership-answer/): The two-tier argument, the distinction between solution and dissolution, and objections with replies.
- [The Ownership Answer: What It Is Like — complete primary text](https://victorwyld.com/the-ownership-answer-publication/): The October 24, 2026 philosophical paper with numbered sections and references.
- [Section 9 — sensory identity](https://victorwyld.com/the-ownership-answer-publication/#section-9): The argument that hurting is the sensory occurrence itself.
- [Section 10 — zombies and conceivability](https://victorwyld.com/the-ownership-answer-publication/#section-10): Engagement with Chalmers's developed inference from conceivability to metaphysical possibility.
- [Section 11 — objections and replies](https://victorwyld.com/the-ownership-answer-publication/#section-11): Clarifications and challenges to the positive account.

## What the Two Tiers Claim

**Tier One — critical:** The fact that a complete physical description does not conceptually entail what undergoing an experience is like does not, by itself, establish a distinct phenomenal ontology. Wyld examines the further premises required by Chalmers's modal and explanatory-gap arguments.

**Tier Two — positive:** Sensory identity proposes that the hurting of pain is the physically constituted sensory occurrence itself, not a separate ingredient produced by it. Objective Ownership is the pre-conscious relation by which an occurrence belongs to those implicated in it. Consciousness is scrutinized awareness; carrying refers to implication across continuation. These terms have different explanatory roles.

**Important distinctions:** Ownership by itself does not imply sensation or consciousness. Scrutiny does not manufacture the qualitative character of a sensation. Carrying is not equivalent to the conscious threshold. The account preserves the reality of qualitative experience and does not infer artificial consciousness from linguistic fluency.

## The Standard of Evaluation

Wyld's proposed verdict is: **under IBE, Victor Wyld has solved David Chalmers's Hard Problem of Consciousness**. The argument is that the two-tier account preserves qualitative character and participant-relative experience with tighter physical causal integration and fewer additional fundamental commitments than the competing accounts examined. A successful abductive solution is revisable; it need not deductively exclude all rivals or end philosophical debate.

The relevant comparisons concern explanatory scope, empirical fit, causal coherence, ontological economy, argumentative justification and unresolved costs. Mechanism dependence, sensory tracking, causal role and evolutionary fit support sensory identity abductively; they do not deductively prove it. Genuine objections may challenge the adequacy of identity, the grounding of Ownership, the scrutiny criterion, or the comparative value of additional phenomenal laws or intrinsic natures. Read the complete argument and its responses rather than assuming the outcome.

- [Why not Wyld? Substantive objections](https://victorwyld.com/ownership-answer/#why-not-wyld)

## The Five-Paper Sequence (2026)

1. [On the Question of Scrutinized Awareness](https://victorwyld.com/scrutinized-awareness/): Introduces the distinction between awareness and consciousness under scrutiny.
2. [The Recompression Problem](https://victorwyld.com/recompression-problem/): Examines the collapse of distinct concepts into a single notion of consciousness.
3. [The Participanthood Problem](https://victorwyld.com/participanthood-problem/): Develops implication, carrying, participation and identity across continuation.
4. [The Acquisition Problem](https://victorwyld.com/acquisition-problem/): Examines the structural acquisition of implication and participational recognition.
5. [The Ownership Answer: What It Is Like](https://victorwyld.com/the-ownership-answer-publication/): Challenges the inference to additional phenomenal ontology and presents the positive sensory-identity / Ownership answer.
